correctness.rationale: Fubini factorizes the box transform into normalized sinc factors. The first axial harmonic vanishes iff that side is a positive integer, when all higher nonzero axial frequencies also vanish. Otherwise the ratio of second to first moduli equals |cos(pi L)|; together with the first modulus, the identity sin^2+cos^2=1 uniquely recovers L>0. The first phase then recovers exp(-2pi i c). Equality of finitely many samples therefore determines all lattice data and the exact integer-factorization and center-residue alias fibers. A strictly decreasing sinc function on (0,1) gives a first-cube counterexample from widths lambda and 3/2, and explicitly identifies the bandwidth-two sharpness. A 43,460-check standard-library numerical script independently exercises the stated formulas, without substituting finite tests for the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 lattice-set sampling theorem establishes full-frequency equidecomposability and sparse-lattice rigidity, not finite all-spectrum determination for arbitrarily long boxes. Inspected finite-rate-of-innovation papers concern unit-period binary intervals or unit-cell image models, without the sharp global box bandwidth-two cutoff and complete positive-integer width/center ambiguity classification. Relevant semantic searches revealed neighboring but mathematically different claims; prior priority remains a risk rather than a certification.
residual_risks: A bibliographic priority risk remains: classical sinc or finite-rate-of-innovation literature may contain an earlier algebraically equivalent finite-box inverse formula.
Some sections of the 2026 motivating HTML could not be reopened for full-paper comparison; this is a material access limit, not evidence of noncoverage.
The theorem is deliberately limited to fixed-axis boxes with exact complex samples; it does not extend to rotated boxes or generic shapes.

value.rationale: The question of how little of the lattice Fourier spectrum determines the rest is natural for exact shape identification. The theorem gives an all-dimensional O(d)-sample exact certificate despite unbounded box widths, proves the coordinate bandwidth threshold cannot be reduced globally for d>=2, and fully classifies intrinsically invisible integer-side geometry. It also isolates the no-wrap first-harmonic regime and provides explicit reconstruction, useful for inverse-sampling design and alias diagnostics. It does not mistake mere formula computation for a universal noise-stability or general-shape theorem.
